  "concepts": [
    { "id": "c-rep", "grounding_span": "specifies and extends the \"Robots Exclusion Protocol\"", "location": "Abstract", "name": "Robots Exclusion Protocol", "aliases": ["REP", "robots.txt protocol"], "description": "Method for service owners to control how content served by their services may be accessed, if at all, by crawlers." },
    { "id": "c-crawler", "grounding_span": "automatic clients known as crawlers", "location": "Abstract", "name": "Crawler", "aliases": ["robot", "bot", "automated client"], "description": "An automated client that recursively accesses URIs; the machine consumer the protocol targets." },
    { "id": "c-robotstxt", "grounding_span": "in a file named \"robots.txt\" as described in", "location": "Section 2.1", "name": "robots.txt file", "aliases": ["/robots.txt"], "description": "The text/plain file at the top-level path of a service that carries the rules and groups of the protocol." },
    { "id": "c-service-owner", "grounding_span": "It may be inconvenient for service owners if crawlers visit the", "location": "Section 1", "name": "Service owner", "aliases": ["site owner"], "description": "Owner of a service providing URI-accessible resources who publishes robots.txt rules." },
    { "id": "c-uri", "grounding_span": "can access through URIs as defined in [RFC3986]", "location": "Section 1", "name": "URI", "aliases": ["Uniform Resource Identifier"], "description": "Identifier for resources a client can access; the object matched against allow/disallow rules." },
    { "id": "c-product-token", "grounding_span": "Crawlers set their own name, which is called a product token, to find", "location": "Section 2.2.1", "name": "Product token", "aliases": [], "description": "The crawler-set name (letters, underscores, hyphens, or '*') used to find the matching group in robots.txt." },
    { "id": "c-user-agent-line", "grounding_span": "startgroupline = *WS \"user-agent\" *WS \":\" *WS product-token EOL", "location": "Section 2.2.1", "name": "User-agent line", "aliases": ["startgroupline"], "description": "The line naming a product token that begins a group." },
    { "id": "c-group", "grounding_span": "Group:  One or more user-agent lines that are followed by one or more", "location": "Section 2.1", "name": "Group", "aliases": [], "description": "One or more user-agent lines followed by one or more rules; terminated by a user-agent line or end of file." },
    { "id": "c-rule", "grounding_span": "Rule:  A line with a key-value pair that defines how a crawler may", "location": "Section 2.1", "name": "Rule", "aliases": [], "description": "A key-value line that defines how a crawler may access URIs." },
    { "id": "c-allow-rule", "grounding_span": "the \"allow\" rule SHOULD be used.", "location": "Section 2.2.2", "name": "Allow rule", "aliases": ["allow line"], "description": "A rule indicating a matching URI path is allowed." },
    { "id": "c-disallow-rule", "grounding_span": "paths in \"allow\" and \"disallow\" rules against the URI", "location": "Section 2.2.2", "name": "Disallow rule", "aliases": ["disallow line"], "description": "A rule indicating a matching URI path is disallowed." },
    { "id": "c-path-matching", "grounding_span": "The matching MUST start with the first", "location": "Section 2.2.2", "name": "Path pattern matching", "aliases": [], "description": "Matching of allow/disallow path patterns against a URI, starting from the first octet of the path." },
    { "id": "c-most-specific-match", "grounding_span": "The most specific match is the match that has the most octets.", "location": "Section 2.2.2", "name": "Most specific / longest match", "aliases": ["longest match"], "description": "The applicable rule is the one whose match has the most octets." },
    { "id": "c-special-characters", "grounding_span": "Crawlers MUST support the following special characters:", "location": "Section 2.2.3", "name": "Special characters", "aliases": ["# $ *"], "description": "The '#' comment, '$' end-of-match, and '*' wildcard characters crawlers must support." },
    { "id": "c-percent-encoding", "grounding_span": "MUST be percent-encoded as defined by [RFC3986] prior to", "location": "Section 2.2.2", "name": "Percent-encoding", "aliases": ["% encoding"], "description": "Encoding of non-ASCII and reserved octets prior to comparison of URI and robots.txt paths." },
    { "id": "c-caching", "grounding_span": "Crawlers MAY cache the fetched robots.txt file's contents.", "location": "Section 2.4", "name": "Caching", "aliases": [], "description": "Optional caching of robots.txt contents, normally for no more than 24 hours." },
    { "id": "c-parsing-limit", "grounding_span": "Crawlers SHOULD impose a parsing limit to protect their systems; see", "location": "Section 2.5", "name": "Parsing limit", "aliases": [], "description": "A byte limit on parsing to protect crawler systems, at least 500 kibibytes." },
    { "id": "c-redirects", "grounding_span": "a server responds to a robots.txt fetch request", "location": "Section 2.3.1.2", "name": "Redirect handling", "aliases": [], "description": "Following at least five consecutive redirects when fetching robots.txt." },
    { "id": "c-unavailable", "grounding_span": "\"Unavailable\" means the crawler tries to fetch the robots.txt file", "location": "Section 2.3.1.3", "name": "\"Unavailable\" status", "aliases": [], "description": "Server status (e.g., HTTP 400-499) indicating robots.txt is unavailable, permitting access to any resources." },
    { "id": "c-complete-disallow", "grounding_span": "MUST assume complete disallow.", "location": "Section 2.3.1.4", "name": "Complete disallow (unreachable)", "aliases": ["Unreachable status"], "description": "When robots.txt is unreachable due to server/network errors, the crawler must assume complete disallow." },
    { "id": "c-parsing-errors", "grounding_span": "Crawlers MUST try to parse each line of the robots.txt file.", "location": "Section 2.3.1.5", "name": "Parsing errors", "aliases": [], "description": "Crawlers must attempt to parse each line and use the parseable rules." },
    { "id": "c-sitemaps", "grounding_span": "for example, \"Sitemaps\" [SITEMAPS].", "location": "Section 2.2.4", "name": "Sitemaps / other records", "aliases": ["other records"], "description": "Records not part of the protocol that crawlers may interpret and which must not terminate a group." },
    { "id": "c-search-engine", "grounding_span": "Search engines, for instance, have", "location": "Section 1", "name": "Search engine", "aliases": [], "description": "A machine consumer that operates crawlers to recursively traverse links for indexing." },
    { "id": "c-access-authorization", "grounding_span": "These rules are not a form of access authorization.", "location": "Section 1", "name": "Access authorization", "aliases": [], "description": "Formal access authorization, which the protocol's rules explicitly are not." },
    { "id": "c-access-control", "grounding_span": "control how content served by their services may be", "location": "Abstract", "name": "Content access control", "aliases": [], "description": "Controlling how and whether content served by a service may be accessed by crawlers." },
    { "id": "c-indexing", "grounding_span": "recursively traverse links for indexing as defined in", "location": "Section 1", "name": "Indexing via link traversal", "aliases": [], "description": "Recursive traversal of links by crawlers for the purpose of indexing." },
    { "id": "c-abnf", "grounding_span": "an Augmented Backus-Naur Form (ABNF) description, as", "location": "Section 2.2", "name": "ABNF formal syntax", "aliases": ["Augmented Backus-Naur Form"], "description": "The formal grammar notation used to define the robots.txt syntax." },
    { "id": "c-case-insensitive-ua", "grounding_span": "Crawlers MUST use case-insensitive matching to find the group that", "location": "Section 2.2.1", "name": "Case-insensitive user-agent matching", "aliases": [], "description": "Product-token/group matching is case-insensitive." },
    { "id": "c-case-sensitive-path", "grounding_span": "The matching SHOULD be case sensitive.", "location": "Section 2.2.2", "name": "Case-sensitive path matching", "aliases": [], "description": "Path matching for allow/disallow rules should be case sensitive." },
    { "id": "c-content-security", "grounding_span": "The Robots Exclusion Protocol is not a substitute for valid content", "location": "Section 3", "name": "Content security measures", "aliases": [], "description": "Application-layer security (e.g., HTTP Authentication) that actually controls access, which robots.txt does not replace." }
